extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users (Overleaf/TeX users) wanting to create vector graphics/diagrams with TikZ
extracted.subtask_description: Practical instructions and idiomatic usage for producing diagrams and graphics in LaTeX using the TikZ package (tikzpicture environment, drawing commands, shapes, nodes, styles, and positioning). Focuses on basic elements and common patterns for constructing figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Load the tikz package in the preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: Include \usepackage{tikz} in the document preamble before drawing any TikZ graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: place \usepackage{tikz} in the preamble of your document. This is required before using the tikzpicture environment or TikZ commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the tikzpicture environment to draw graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw all TikZ graphics inside a tikzpicture environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows \begin{tikzpicture} ... \end{tikzpicture}. Note: the tikzfigure environment can be enclosed inside a figure or similar environment (see 'Inserting Images') if you want floats/ captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminate drawing commands with a semicolon
rubrics_metrics.description: Every draw/fill/filldraw/node command must end with a semicolon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page stresses: "It's important to notice the semicolon ; used at the end of each draw command." Omitting it breaks the command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify paths using endpoints and -- for straight segments
rubrics_metrics.description: Define straight lines and polygon edges by giving coordinate endpoints and joining them with --.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw[gray, thick] (-1,2) -- (2,-4);. Bracketed options (e.g., gray, thick) set attributes such as color and stroke thickness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use filldraw / fill / draw appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: \filldraw draws a shape and fills it; \fill fills without (necessarily) drawing an outer stroke; \draw draws outlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \filldraw[black] (0,0) circle (2pt) creates a filled black circle. Use \fill when you don't need an outer stroke; use \draw when you only want an outline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create points as small circles with radius units
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent points by drawing a small circle at a coordinate with an explicit radius (e.g. 2pt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \filldraw[gray] (0,0) circle (2pt); declares centre (0,0) and radius (2pt). Units such as pt, mm are used for radii and lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add text with nodes and anchor them
rubrics_metrics.description: Use node[...] {text} to place text boxes, and use anchors like node[anchor=west] to position relative to a point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: node[anchor=west]{Intersection point} places a box anchored at the west of the referenced coordinate. Nodes are boxes containing text and can be empty to show nothing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and use node styles via ./.style=
rubrics_metrics.description: Pass named style definitions (e.g., roundnode/.style={...}) to the tikzpicture environment to reuse formatting for nodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: roundnode/.style={circle, draw=green!60, fill=green!5, very thick, minimum size=7mm}. Styles can set shape, draw/fill colours, thickness, minimum size, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare nodes with identifiers for later reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Create nodes with \node[style] (id) {content}; so they can be referenced later for positioning and connecting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \node[squarednode] (maintopic) {2}; gives the node the id 'maintopic'. Leaving braces empty yields no displayed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the positioning library for relative node placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Load \usetikzlibrary{positioning} to enable the [above=of <id>] and related syntaxes for relative placement of nodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \node[roundnode] (uppercircle) [above=of maintopic] {1}; Without the positioning library you can use 'above of=maintopic' but the positioning library allows '[above=3cm of maintopic]' to control distances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference node anchors when drawing between nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: When connecting nodes, reference specific anchors like (node.south) or (node.north) to control where lines attach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw[->] (uppercircle.south) -- (maintopic.north); uses named node anchors to draw an arrow between specific points on nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw Bézier curves with .. controls .. syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the .. controls (c1) and (c2) .. syntax to draw cubic Bézier curves defined by two endpoints and two control points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw (-2,2) .. controls (-1,0) and (1,0) .. (2,2); The endpoints are (-2,2) and (2,2); (-1,0) and (1,0) are control points that determine curvature (described as 'attractor points').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use relative control vectors +(dir:len) for curved connections
rubrics_metrics.description: In control points you can use relative offsets like +(down:7mm) and +(right:7mm) to define control directions and distances from anchors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: .. controls +(down:7mm) and +(right:7mm) .. (lowercircle.east); This specifies control points relative to the current node anchor position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create circles and specify stroke/fill and thickness
rubrics_metrics.description: Use (center) circle (radius) along with options color=..., fill=..., and thickness keywords to define appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \filldraw[color=red!60, fill=red!5, very thick] (-1,0) circle (1.5); color=red!60 sets ring colour, fill=red!5 sets interior, very thick sets stroke width. See reference guide for available colours and thickness values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create ellipses with horizontal and vertical radii
rubrics_metrics.description: Use (center) ellipse (xradius and yradius) to draw ellipses; choose fill/draw based on whether you need an outline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \fill[blue!50] (2.5,0) ellipse (1.5 and 0.5); The two numbers are horizontal and vertical radii respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw arcs with arc(start: end: radius) syntax and arrows
rubrics_metrics.description: Use arc(start: end: radius) to draw circular arcs; include -> in options to place an arrowhead at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw[ultra thick, ->] (6.5,0) arc (0:220:1); provides starting/ending angles and radius in the format (0:220:1). The -> option gives an arrow at the end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw rectangles using the rectangle operator with two corners
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the special rectangle keyword and provide two diagonally opposite points to create a rectangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw[blue, very thick] (0,0) rectangle (3,2); The first point is the starting corner and the second is the opposite corner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct polygons via sequences of -- and close with cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Build closed polygonal shapes by chaining coordinates with -- and use the cycle instruction to close the path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw (4,0) -- (6,0) -- (5.7,2) -- cycle; cycle closes the path by connecting the end to the start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify colors using the 'color=...' and 'fill=...' syntax and mixing (e.g., red!60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set stroke and fill colors with key=value options; tikz supports color mixing syntax like red!60 for tints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: color=red!60 sets the ring colour to 60% red while fill=red!5 fills with a very light red. The page refers to the reference guide and 'Using colours in LaTeX' for more colours and custom definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose thickness keywords from predefined values
rubrics_metrics.description: Use thickness keywords such as ultra thin, very thin, thin, thick, very thick, ultra thick to set stroke width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reference lists thickness parameter values (ultra thin ... ultra thick). Use these tokens in the options bracket, e.g., [very thick].

rubrics_metrics.name: Use explicit coordinates and units for positions and dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide coordinate pairs (x,y) for positions and use explicit units for dimensions (e.g., 2pt, 7mm) when specifying radii, offsets, or distances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples throughout: (0,0) coordinates, circle (2pt), +(down:7mm) relative offsets. Units like pt and mm are demonstrated; consistent units help control sizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine basic elements (nodes, lines, paths) to form diagrams
rubrics_metrics.description: Build diagrams by defining node styles/positions and connecting them with lines/curves/arcs using the drawing primitives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The diagrams example shows defining roundnode/squarednode styles, declaring nodes with positions, then drawing arrows and curved connections to form a labeled diagram. Use libraries and styles to manage complexity and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed TikZ figures within LaTeX float environments when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: TikZ figures (tikzpicture) can be placed inside figure or similar float environments to gain captions and floating behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: The tikzfigure environment can be enclosed inside a figure or similar environment. See the 'Inserting Images' article for more about figures and floats.
